key_insight: A magnetic-field-induced hydrodynamic potential modifies ion distributions in flowing electrolytes, producing a Hall potential that is nearly linear in flow velocity and magnetic field strength but largely independent of salt concentration.
engineering_relevance: The framework could inform magnetic control and interpretation of ion transport in microfluidic channels and electrochemical systems.
method: Analytically couple steady-state Navier–Stokes, Nernst–Planck, and Poisson equations for unidirectional electrolyte flow.
Derive ion distributions incorporating electrostatic and hydrodynamic potentials, then apply them to Poiseuille and counterion-only flows.
Analyze two-dimensional entrance transients to assess the one-dimensional framework.
evidence_signal: Theoretical analysis predicts rapid Hall-field and space-charge adjustment versus a much longer, Péclet-dependent salt-concentration wake; the abstract reports no experimental validation.
watch_item: Applicability beyond dilute electrolytes and steady unidirectional flow requires further assessment, especially near channel entrances.
paper_title: Theory of magneto-electrokinetics in unidirectional electrolyte flow: Hydrodynamic potential and Hall effect
